report_name: U.S. Senate Passes Bipartisan Healthcare Cybersecurity Act

identities.name: U.S. Senate
identities.description: The legislative body that unanimously passed the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act.

identities.name: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
identities.description: A U.S. federal agency tasked with improving coordination with CISA, developing a cybersecurity incident response plan, and modernizing HIPAA rules under the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act.

identities.name: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
identities.description: A U.S. federal agency whose collaboration with HHS is set to be improved by the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act to streamline incident response and information sharing.

identities.name: U.S. healthcare providers
identities.description: The primary beneficiaries and affected parties of the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act, with a special emphasis on small, under-resourced, and rural facilities.

identities.name: Mark Warner
identities.description: A U.S. Senator who co-sponsored the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act.

identities.name: Bill Cassidy
identities.description: A U.S. Senator who co-sponsored the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act.

identities.name: House of Representatives
identities.description: The legislative body where the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act will be considered following its passage in the Senate.

identities.name: HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR)
identities.description: The HHS office mentioned as a potential future enforcer of modernized HIPAA security measures.

relationships.source_name: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
